title: Sprint-bundling & capacity-hedge playbook for quarterly hosted API + model catalog
creator: Leah Thomson
description:
Objective: Create an operational playbook that bundles quarterly sprint work (feature rollouts, model rotations, infra changes) into lanes that explicitly hedge hosting capacity and model-quality risk for the Hosted API and curated model catalog. This playbook must be prescriptive enough for PMs to run planning sessions, for Eng to evaluate capacity impact, and for Console/Observability teams to surface readiness signals.

Why: We consistently see tight coupling between model lineup decisions and short-term capacity pressure (burst/GPU allocations, canary windows). Without an explicit bundling and hedging process, rollouts create last-minute tradeoffs that increase latency/regression risk. This ticket produces a repeatable cadence for quarterly planning to reduce surprises and create measurable rollback/fallback paths.

Scope: Hosted API endpoints and the model catalog rotation schedule for the upcoming quarter (including new variants and quantized builds), relevant infra changes that affect serving (autoscale policy, batching tweaks), and the rollouts/runway for canaries and feature gates. Excludes long-term model research and unrelated infra incidents.

Playbook summary (high level steps):
1) Intake & triage: PMs collect all candidate items for the quarter (catalog swaps, new endpoints, SKU changes). Each item must include a short risk assessment (latency, cost, QA delta).
2) Scenario mapping: For each item, define three runtime scenarios (nominal traffic, 2x burst, fallback failure) and quantify expected token throughput impact and latency delta.
3) Bundling into lanes: Group items into 3 lanes (Green: low-risk, Blue: controlled rollout, Red: heavy-impact). Each lane has a capacity budget and a canary window profile.
4) Capacity hedge: Assign hedges (reserved burst capacity, alternative model variant, traffic-splitting route) to each lane. For Red items require a documented fallback variant and decaying traffic policy.
5) Canary & observability contract: Define per-item SLOs (P95 latency, error rate, quality regression thresholds) and required dashboards/evals. Canary windows must include automated rollback triggers.
6) Cross-team sign-off: PM, Eng (runtime + infra), DX/Console, and Research sign-off checklist before commit to the lane.
7) Execution & weekly checks: During the quarter, weekly execution board with capacity burn, canary outcomes, and quality regressions.
8) Post-mortem & runway update: After each lane completes, capture learnings and adjust next quarter's hedging coefficients.

Deliverables:
- A one-page lane template (fields: item id, owner, lane, capacity delta, fallback variant, canary window, SLOs).
- Capacity estimation spreadsheet populated by Eng (tokens/sec, expected GPU-hours).
- Canary checklist and automated rollback rule set in Console.
- Runbook for switching to fallback variant with runbook links for on-call.

Acceptance criteria:
- PMs can produce a quarter plan with all items assigned to lanes and hedges for 90% of items.
- Eng provides capacity estimate for each lane that aligns with historical traffic within +/- 25%.
- Canary contract defined for each Blue/Red item and existing tests wired into CI to run the canned prompt suite.
- Dashboard templates (latency, error, cost-per-token) created in Console and linked to each item.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Underestimating traffic bursts. Mitigation: conservative 2x burst scenario and dedicated short-term burst pool for Red lane.
- Risk: Quality regression escapes canary. Mitigation: expanded eval set for canaries + manual gating for high-customer-impact endpoints.
- Risk: Too many Red items in one quarter. Mitigation: enforce lane capacity budget and cross-team veto on lane oversubscription.
